subject: Backpressure & capacity allocator playtest — ACME VPC private pool

Subject: Strange throughput collapse during sustained 5k QPS run

Hi Grace / Vivek,

We ran the sustained 5k QPS playtest in our VPC yesterday and hit a ~35% throughput collapse after about 12 minutes despite capacity showing available GPUs in the pool. Latency spikes first, then tokens/sec drops and we see a surge of queued requests on our side. Attached are the traces and a short CSV with time-series metrics.

Key observations from our SRE:
- Token generation per-GPU decreased while GPU utilization stayed 60-70%.
- There were repeated admission-control rejections from the allocator followed by a flood of retries.
- Network egress was stable; we suspect an allocator backpressure loop + cache warmup miss storm.

Can Redwood review the allocator behavior and recommend tuning or a short-term mitigation? We can run another test this week.

Attachments: playtest-backpressure-traces.csv, kvcache-warmup-log.txt

Thanks,
Ravi Verma
ACME SRE

Subject: Re: Strange throughput collapse during sustained 5k QPS run

On Oct 18, 2026, at 09:12, Ops Team <ops@acme.com> wrote:
> We ran the sustained 5k QPS playtest in our VPC yesterday and hit a ~35% throughput collapse after about 12 minutes despite capacity showing available GPUs in the pool.

Preliminary notes from the allocator logs and trace replay:
- We reproduced the pattern in our staging replay. The allocator starts rejecting admission for short windows when the per-GPU token generation latency jumps (seen at ~11:30 into the run). Rejections cluster with retry storms on the client side.
- Cause appears to be a combination of:
  1) KV cache cold misses at scale — many requests touch different prefixes so effective cache hit rate drops.
  2) Admission-control configured to be conservative on sustained per-node latency; the short rejections cause clients to retry aggressively and that transient spike cascades.
  3) Batching dynamics: when the runtime switches quantization kernel paths (on certain sequence lengths) we see per-step latency variance that trips the quantile-based admission heuristics.

Data we attached: allocator-event-heatmap (allocator-heatmap.png), time-series traces (playtest-backpressure-traces.csv). Also included a short KV warmup log excerpt (kvcache-warmup-log.txt).

Short-term mitigations to propose for the next customer run (non-breaking):
- Relax the admission control threshold for sustained runs by +15% and increase allowed burst window from 30s -> 90s.
- Add client-side jittered exponential backoff on 429s with max backoff 750ms (reduces retry flood).
- Pre-warm KV cache by issuing targeted prefix warmup for top-10k prefixes during warmup window.

Medium-term changes (we should schedule):
- Admission controller: add hysteresis and detection of retry-flood patterns (differentiate organic load from retries).
- Batching policy: introduce sequence-length aware kernel pinning to avoid switching quantization kernel mid-run for hot sequences.
- Metrics: surface per-prefix cache hit rate and per-batch kernel-switch counters into Console to make these failures searchable.

I'll draft a tuning matrix (thresholds, warmup cadence) and a playbook for ACME. Dylan — can you run the playtest replay with the relaxed thresholds and attach the run artifacts?

— Vivek
VP, Runtime Engineering
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-19T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Backpressure & capacity allocator playtest — ACME VPC private pool

Attached is the replay we ran with the proposed relaxed thresholds and client backoff simulated. Results (summary):
- No throughput collapse observed in the 20-minute sustained 5k replay. Aggregate tokens/sec stayed within 8% of baseline.
- Retry spikes reduced by ~6x due to jittered backoff.
- KV warmup cut the cold-miss tail; hit rate improved from 38% -> 72% after a 3-minute targeted warmup.

Artifacts attached: allocator-heatmap.png, replay-runlog.txt, playtest-backpressure-traces.csv (updated).

Open action items:
- Rishi: add a Console alert for per-prefix cache-hit drop below 50% during a sustained-run window.
- Grace: propose a conservative rollout plan to ACME: 1) enable relaxed thresholds for staged runs, 2) enable auto-warmup for known hot prefixes, 3) ship a retry-guidance snippet for client SDKs.

I'll link the replay artifacts in the shared Drive shortly.

— Dylan
